doc.headline: Run every planner with a retry; past that, picking a model is an unpriced trade in which each extra point of pass rate costs more, steepest for Atlas-M.
doc.lede: With a retry, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} passes {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} for {cost_per_month.brisk-s.low.r1} a month; {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} passes {compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.difference|abs} points more for {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.monthly|abs} more a month. A declared pass-rate floor or price per point would turn this trade into a decision.
doc.flag: Nothing was declared in advance: no control, no floor, no price per point. The planner's owner makes this call, after settling what the monthly volume counts.

caveats.material_if: only once the owner sets a floor or a price per point: that line then picks the option, and the lean below holds only if it lands in the lean's band.

only for gaps whose interval sits near zero: every gap here is read unpaired, which errs wide, so a paired re-read could separate Brisk-S's high reasoning from its low, but would not undo a gap already clear of zero.

only for thin leads, and Atlas-M at high reasoning with a retry is the thin lead it means: the top of {n_candidates|words} configurations, ahead of the lean by an uncorrected interval whose low end is {compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.low} points, so its true lead may be smaller or nil. The lean holds either way, since it rests on what each point costs, not on beating Atlas-M.

caveats.label: Cost routing unknown
caveats.material_if: only if another provider serves these models at other prices: no configuration names who served it, so the cost order, every cost multiple between models and every price on the page hold for this run's routing only.

caveats.label: Monthly volume's unit unstated
caveats.material_if: only if the declared {meta.volume_per_month} a month counts tasks rather than calls: then every monthly cost, every price per point and every band in the explore rows grows by the configurations' calls per task, between {measure.calls_per_task.atlas-m.high.r1.mean} and {measure.calls_per_task.nano-xs.off.r1.mean} on the frontier, and an owner pricing a point against today's bands could land in the wrong one. The owner should settle the unit before pricing.

decision.text: Cost against pass rate. The cheapest configuration, {arm:nano-xs.off.r0}, passes {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.off.r0.mean} for {cost_per_month.nano-xs.off.r0} a month; the highest, {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}, passes {measure.pass_rate.atlas-m.high.r1.mean} for {cost_per_month.atlas-m.high.r1}. Every option between them on the frontier runs with a retry.

Each step up the frontier costs more per point a month: {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} from {arm:nano-xs.high.r1} to {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} on to {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, and {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} on to {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}. These prices are point estimates; the last two steps buy gains this run cannot tell from zero. Every band is listed under What you could change.

Ours, not a declared rule: {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, for a point worth between {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month. It is clearly ahead of {arm:nano-xs.high.r1} (interval {compare.brisk-s.low.r1.nano-xs.high.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval} points), and the next step up buys a gain not separated from zero.

{arm:atlas-m.high.r1} is ahead of the lean, with an interval of {compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval} points that clears zero only narrowly, read unpaired and uncorrected across {n_candidates|words} configurations, at {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} its cost at this run's unnamed routing. No margin or floor was declared, so no option sits near a line.

A declaration first: the owner settles what the monthly volume counts, then sets a pass-rate floor or a price per point. Then a re-run of Brisk-S at high against low reasoning, both with a retry, at {settle.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.cases_needed_80} cases each (the size for independent arms; fewer if paired on the same cases), tells them apart four times in five.

claims.text: Cost and pass rate trade along one frontier: from {arm:nano-xs.off.r0} to {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}, cost per thousand calls rises {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.nano-xs.off.r0.multiple} at this run's unnamed routing, and {count.frontier.pass_rate|words} configurations sit on it.

evidence.caption: Cost per thousand calls, on a log scale, against pass rate for every configuration, at this run's unnamed provider routing; the table below names the frontier's configurations.
The frontier configurations in order, each step with its price per point of pass rate a month; point estimates at the declared volume.

claims.text: A retry lifts pass rate for every model, most where the model is weakest: {lever.retry.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.effect} points for {arm:nano-xs.off.r0}, against {lever.retry.atlas-m.high.r0.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.effect} for {arm:atlas-m.high.r0}, the only pairing whose interval reaches zero. At this run's unnamed routing it adds at most {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r0.per_1k|abs} per thousand calls.

evidence.caption: Pass-rate gain from adding a retry, in points, with unpaired intervals, for one configuration per model.
The same gain for another configuration per model; the remaining pairings' rates, without intervals, are in Every arm by measure.

claims.text: At the top, neither the bigger model nor more reasoning is told apart on its own: with a retry, Brisk-S trails Atlas-M by {lever.model.atlas-m.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.effect|abs} points at low reasoning, and high reasoning adds {lever.reasoning.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.effect} for Brisk-S; both intervals cross zero. At this run's unnamed routing, Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} as much at the same settings.

evidence.caption: Effect of switching model or raising reasoning among the retry configurations of Atlas-M and Brisk-S, in points, with unpaired intervals.

claims.text: Model and reasoning set the median latency; the retry leaves the median unchanged in every pair shown and lengthens the slow tail, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} reading {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} at p95 against {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r0.p95} without it. No latency budget was declared.

evidence.caption: Latency from median to p95 for every frontier configuration beside its twin with or without a retry.

claims.text: Multi-hop questions are the weakest task for each of the three frontier options shown; the lean passes {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} there against {task.single.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} on single lookups.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task; the snapshot states no case count per task, so these rows carry no interval and are descriptive.

claims.text: The lean's kept failures each break differently: a multi-hop question collapsed into one search, a date window off by a day, and an ambiguous name searched instead of asked about. The snapshot does not say how many failures they were kept from.

evidence.caption: Every failure the snapshot keeps for the lean, one per task where kept; a sample, not a count.

method.text: Each of the {n_candidates|words} configurations ran {scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases} cases with no lost or failed trials; repeats are not stated. Configurations cross {count.levels.model|words} models, {count.levels.reasoning|words} reasoning levels, and a retry or none.

The pipeline's pass or fail grade on each planned query. Failures are classed as a missing call, wrong arguments, the wrong tool or malformed output; the snapshot defines pass no further. On ambiguous entities the expected answer is a clarifying question.

Read at {lever.retry.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.level} from each configuration's binomial spread over its cases and combined as if the configurations ran different cases, which errs wide; uncorrected for the number of comparisons. Per-task figures carry none.
Cost per thousand calls as measured, at a provider routing no configuration names. Monthly figures use the declared {meta.volume_per_month} a month, whose unit the campaign does not state.
Median and p95 per configuration; no budget was declared.
No control and no criteria were declared, so no option is read against a line.

findings.finding: Brisk-S at low reasoning without a retry (95.3% at $0.288 per 1k calls) is not dominated: no other configuration is both cheaper and better. It sits above the seven configurations the frontier claim counts, and a pass-rate floor between 94.9% and 95.3% makes it the cheapest option that meets the floor. Yet the headline says 'run every planner with a retry', and the floor row says only 'up to 98%, a Brisk-S one'. Say in the frontier claim or the floor row that the seven are the price-per-point frontier, and that this no-retry configuration is cheapest only for a floor of 94.9% to 95.3%, where it saves about $56 a month against the lean for 1.8 fewer points. Or soften the headline to 'every option on the price-per-point frontier runs with a retry'.

The lede compares Brisk-S and Atlas-M costs ('$1,208 a month', '$12,700 more a month') with no routing qualifier. 'The trade' and 'Where the answer flips' in the decision block also price models without one. The confidence line covers 'every price on the page', so a reader is not misled. Still, add 'at this run's unnamed provider routing' to the lede's cost sentence, as the claims and Watch now do. Also, in the cost-routing confidence clause, say why the lean holds until the routing is known: for example, a routing change would have to shift the roughly 2.7 times cost gap between Nano-XS at high reasoning and Brisk-S at low reasoning enough to move the band edges. Watch's '12 times' is 11.5 times on the figures ($3.477 against $0.302).

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and the frontier claim tell a reader what to do now: run every planner with a retry. They also say what is still open, which model to run, and the reason: nothing is declared, so it is a trade the owner has to price. The lean is Brisk-S at low reasoning with a retry, at 97.1% for $1,208 a month. The Watch line names the main risk: Atlas-M at high reasoning with a retry is ahead by 1.5 points (+0.3 to +2.6) at 12 times the cost. The step prices match price_tradeoff: $319.67, $1,595.18 and $17,236.36 a point a month.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims build on each other. The frontier claim gives seven configurations on the frontier, which matches price_tradeoff. The retry claim shows every frontier step past the cheapest runs with a retry. The top claim shows that model alone and reasoning alone do not separate, while the Watch line shows the two together do (+1.5, +0.3 to +2.6). These fit. Each block's rows match its sentence. Only one pairing, Atlas-M high, has a retry interval reaching zero (-0.2 to +2.0); Brisk-S high just clears it (+0.04 to +2.6). Multi-hop is the lowest task for S, J and F. One rough spot: the latency claim opens with 'not the retry', yet its own rows show the retry raising p95 in every pair, from 378 to 450 ms and from 2430 to 2551 ms.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The lean's weak points are visible: multi-hop at 95.6%, its kept failures, and the 0.8-point gain from high reasoning that this run cannot tell from zero. Two things read stronger than the evidence allows. Watch calls Atlas-M at high reasoning 'clearly ahead' on an interval whose low end is +0.3. That interval is unpaired and uncorrected, and Atlas-M is the best of 18 configurations, which is the case the best-of-n caveat describes. And the top claim's 'Atlas-M costs 5.5 times as much' ranks the models by cost with no routing caveat on the claim.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing left out would change the decision. Brisk-S at low reasoning without a retry is undominated on the two axes (95.3% at $0.288), but it sits under the frontier hull, and the lean costs only about $56 a month more for 1.8 points. With the volume read as tasks, cost per task keeps the same frontier order. Two items in the left-out list point to an appendix effects table that does not exist (see findings).

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The page names all four confounds: no control (unpaired intervals), best of many, unknown cost routing and the volume unit. Each has a next step. But the routing caveat is attached only to the frontier claim. The retry claim ($0.077 per thousand calls) and the top claim (5.5 times the cost) cite costs without it. The volume clause says the cost gaps between models 'would not close'. It leaves out that the explore bands the owner is told to pick from would scale by about 1.5 times. For example, the lean's band would become roughly $490 to $2,450 a point.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an action and what it would settle. The owner declares a floor or a price per point. The Brisk-S high-against-low re-run is sized from settle_cases: 5,432 cases for four in five, and 9.4% wrong-side today. The multi-hop work and the provider and unit record are also there. A small slip: the re-run is called paired on the same cases, but 5,432 is the size for independent arms.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The retry, top and tasks blocks fit their claims and carry the claims' own figures. The frontier claim says 'seven configurations sit on it', but its values table lists all 18 points and does not mark which seven, so a reader cannot check the claim from the block. The latency caption says 'the frontier configurations and their no-retry twins', but the block leaves out three frontier configurations (Nano-XS off without and with a retry, Nano-XS low with a retry) and Brisk-S high without a retry, which is the lean-adjacent L's twin.

findings.finding: 'Atlas-M costs 5.5 times as much at the same settings' ranks two models by cost, but the claim names no provider and carries only the no-control caveat. No configuration records who served it, and the page's own 'Cost routing unknown' caveat says the cost order holds only for this run's routing. Attach 'Cost routing unknown' to this claim and write it as 'at this run's unnamed provider routing, Atlas-M costs 5.5 times as much'. Do the same in the retry claim, which cites '$0.077 per thousand calls'.

Watch says Atlas-M · reasoning high · 1 retry is 'clearly ahead' of the lean, on an interval of +0.3 to +2.6 points. That interval is unpaired and uncorrected across 18 configurations, and Atlas-M is the top one, which is exactly where the best-of-n caveat applies. Say 'ahead, with an interval clearing zero by 0.3 points, uncorrected for 18 configurations'. Also make the best-of-n confidence clause say whether this lead is the thin lead it means, and why the lean holds either way. Right now it only says the pass rates 'likely fall a little'.

The explore row for the worth of a point gives only three bands: below $3.20 (Nano-XS off, no retry), $319.67 to $1,595.18 (the lean) and above $17,236.36 (Atlas-M high with a retry). It leaves out the bands for Nano-XS off with a retry ($3.20 to $17.31), Nano-XS low with a retry ($17.31 to $111.22), Nano-XS high with a retry ($111.22 to $319.67) and Brisk-S high with a retry ($1,595.18 to $17,236.36). That last band is the widest on the page. An owner who prices a point anywhere in those ranges gets no answer. List all seven bands, since the first next step says 'the explore bands then pick one'.

The claim says seven configurations sit on the frontier, but the values table lists all 18 points and marks only J. Add a column or tag for the seven frontier points (Nano-XS off without and with a retry, Nano-XS low and high with a retry, Brisk-S low and high with a retry, Atlas-M high with a retry), so a reader can check the count against the block.

The opening 'Latency follows model and reasoning, not the retry' is contradicted in part by the block: the retry raises p95 in every pair shown (378 to 450 ms, 465 to 513 ms, 2430 to 2551 ms). Write it as 'the retry leaves the median unchanged and adds 48 to 121 ms at p95'. The caption also says 'the frontier configurations and their no-retry twins', but Nano-XS off without and with a retry, Nano-XS low with a retry, and Brisk-S high without a retry (L's twin) are missing. Add them or reword the caption to match what is drawn.

The volume-unit confidence clause says only that the cost gaps between models 'would not close'. If the 4,000,000 a month counts tasks, every price per point on the page and every explore band scales by about 1.45 to 1.9 times, depending on the configuration's calls per task. The lean's band, for example, becomes about $490 to $2,450. An owner setting a price per point against these bands could land in the wrong one. Say this in the clause and in the explore row, or ask the owner to resolve the unit before pricing.

The decision block and the second next step call the Brisk-S high-against-low re-run paired, on the same fresh cases, at 5,432 cases each. That size comes from reading the two arms as independent. A paired design over the same cases needs fewer. Either call it the unpaired size and add 'fewer if paired', or size it paired. In the multi-hop next step, also say that the re-test must record case counts per task, because today's task figures carry no interval and cannot show a gap closing.

The retry block's caption says 'the other pairings are in the appendix', and the left-out list says the model and reasoning effects have a 'full table in the appendix'. The appendix has no effects table, only per-arm figures. Add the nine retry pairings and the model and reasoning effects to the appendix, or reword both pointers to say the reader can compute them from 'Every arm by measure'.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Each confound is carried into the story and the next steps. Unknown cost routing is on every claim that cites a cost, with a next step to record providers.
